hints: Form two independent directions in plane $ABC$, such as $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}$.
Find a normal $(a,b,c)$ perpendicular to both directions using scalar products or their cross product.
Use one of $A,B,C$ in $ax+by+cz=d$ to determine $d$.
Verify the resulting equation with the other two points.
walkthrough:
Find two non-parallel vectors in the plane containing $A(1, 3, 2)$, $B(2, 1, -1)$ and $C(2, 4, 1)$:
$$\overrightarrow{AB} = \overrightarrow{OB} - \overrightarrow{OA} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\\\ 1 \\\\ -1 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\\\ 3 \\\\ 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\\\ -2 \\\\ -3 \end{pmatrix}$$
$$\overrightarrow{AC} = \overrightarrow{OC} - \overrightarrow{OA} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\\\ 4 \\\\ 1 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\\\ 3 \\\\ 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\\\ 1 \\\\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Compute the normal vector $\mathbf{n}$ to the plane by calculating the vector product $\overrightarrow{AB} \times \overrightarrow{AC}$:
$$\mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\\\ -2 \\\\ -3 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\\\ 1 \\\\ -1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} (-2)(-1) - (-3)(1) \\\\ (-3)(1) - (1)(-1) \\\\ (1)(1) - (-2)(1) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 + 3 \\\\ -3 + 1 \\\\ 1 + 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\\\ -2 \\\\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$$
Write the Cartesian equation of the plane in the form $\mathbf{r} \cdot \mathbf{n} = d$, which gives $5x - 2y + 3z = d$.

Substitute the coordinates of point $A(1, 3, 2)$ into the equation to determine $d$:
$$d = 5(1) - 2(3) + 3(2) = 5 - 6 + 6 = 5$$

State the equation of the plane:
$$5x - 2y + 3z = 5$$

hints: Write the line through $D=(-3,1,2)$ with direction $\overrightarrow{OA}=(1,3,2)$.
Substitute its general coordinates into $x+2y-z=7$ and solve for the line parameter.
Use that parameter to obtain the position vector of $P$.
Since $\overrightarrow{DP}$ is the parameter multiple of $(1,3,2)$, use its magnitude to show the stated length.
walkthrough:
Identify the direction vector of the line through $D(-3, 1, 2)$ parallel to $\overrightarrow{OA} = \mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j} + 2\mathbf{k}$:
$$\mathbf{d} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\\\ 3 \\\\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$$

Write the vector equation of this line with parameter $\lambda$:
$$\mathbf{r} = \begin{pmatrix} -3 \\\\ 1 \\\\ 2 \end{pmatrix} + \lambda\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\\\ 3 \\\\ 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -3 + \lambda \\\\ 1 + 3\lambda \\\\ 2 + 2\lambda \end{pmatrix}$$

Substitute the coordinates of a general point on the line into the plane equation $x + 2y - z = 7$:
$$(-3 + \lambda) + 2(1 + 3\lambda) - (2 + 2\lambda) = 7$$
$$-3 + \lambda + 2 + 6\lambda - 2 - 2\lambda = 7$$
$$5\lambda - 3 = 7 \implies 5\lambda = 10 \implies \lambda = 2$$

Substitute $\lambda = 2$ into the parametric equations of the line to obtain the position vector of $P$:
$$\overrightarrow{OP} = \begin{pmatrix} -3 + 2 \\\\ 1 + 3(2) \\\\ 2 + 2(2) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -1 \\\\ 7 \\\\ 6 \end{pmatrix} = -\mathbf{i} + 7\mathbf{j} + 6\mathbf{k}$$

Calculate the length of the line segment $DP$ using the vector magnitude formula:
$$|\overrightarrow{DP}| = \sqrt{2^2 + 6^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{4 + 36 + 16} = \sqrt{56}$$
